recipe.notes:
The Gemma 4 MoE judge (8 active of 128 experts, vision encoder ~550M params). Client block: no temperature, NO extra_body sampling (owner answer 3: the catalog's convention wins over the cards' temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 64; to opt in, `--set judge.temperature=1.0 --set judge.extra_body='{"top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 64}'`), max_output_tokens 16384, context_tokens 131072 (owner answer 4), concurrency 256, decoding json_schema, image_processor gemma4 (patch 16, pooling 3, max_soft_tokens 280; the client reproduces the engine's resize, no --mm-processor-kwargs pin), max_images 10, max_videos 0. Thinking OFF by default, thinking on as a declared client choice (owner answer 2; see the 12B family's note for the mechanism: `--set judge.extra_body='{"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}}'`). Video via `wire: frames` only (owner answer 5); audio is not part of these checkpoints and is out of scope (owner answer 8). The two variants' judge-shaped render is byte-identical (owner answer 1): Google's canonical template (18683 B, sha256 prefix ae53464bf3be2580) and NVIDIA's re-export (16934 B, sha256 prefix 94899c0f917d93f6) differ only on tool-call, null-argument and multi-turn-thinking paths a single-turn judge request never reaches; the NVIDIA tokenizer_config.json's missing response_template block is read by nothing in vLLM v0.31.0 (the answer schema comes from the request). Memory arithmetic, both GPU classes (GiB, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92). Shared KV shape: 5 full layers x 2 x 2 global KV heads x 512 head_dim x <dtype> B per token; 25 sliding layers hold their 1024-token window. - bf16 (51 611 872 412 B on disk, 2 shards; 48.07 GiB weights): TP1 -> KV 5 x 2 x 2 x 512 x 2 B = 20 480
  B/token (a 32k window 0.625 GiB) + sliding 25 x 1024 x 2 x 8 x 256 x 2 B = 0.195 GiB/sequence -> a 32k
  window 0.82 GiB. B200 (192 GB; 0.92 -> 164.51 GiB): 164.51 - 48.07 = 116.44 GiB cache -> ~142 concurrent
  32k windows. H100 (80 GB; 0.92 -> 68.55 GiB): 68.55 - 48.07 = 20.48 GiB -> ~25 concurrent 32k windows.
  resources.gpus: 1 for both classes; the catalog's TP2 block was written before decision 41 (TP2 halves the
  weights but needs two GPUs, and one TP1 replica per GPU is the better packing).
- NVFP4 (18 782 360 732 B on disk, 2 shards; 17.49 GiB weights; experts only: 11 520 quantised tensors = 30
  layers x 128 experts x 3 projections; dense mlp/router/self_attn, lm_head, embed_vision and the vision
  tower excluded): TP1 -> KV (fp8) 5 x 2 x 2 x 512 x 1 B = 10 240 B/token (a 32k window 0.31 GiB) + sliding
  25 x 1024 x 2 x 8 x 256 x 1 B = 0.098 GiB -> a 32k window 0.41 GiB. B200: 164.51 - 17.49 = 147.02 GiB ->
  ~358 windows. H100: 68.55 - 17.49 = 51.06 GiB -> ~124 windows. The NVFP4 card's own constraint ("vLLM
  works with TP=1 only, it does support EP") matches the decision-41 shape; a TP2/EP attempt is an E2 probe,
  not the default (owner answer 7: the E2 wave records the chosen MoE backend, VLLM_CUTLASS/Marlin on
  Hopper or a FlashInfer/TRTLLM backend on Blackwell, and any Marlin W4A16 fallback).
Engine support: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration is in vLLM v0.31.0's registry (registry.py:418, module gemma4_mm); both pins were checked 2026-10-09. status: unverified until the E2 judge wave passes.

The bf16 release (the family's reference point; the NVFP4 variant is its quantised sibling). B200 and H100: TP1 (resources.gpus 1). The served name is the recipe id; the T4 scenarios override it to their slot name at run time.
